license_note: The Kolibri-1 model card states that "The model weights are published by Aleph Alpha GmbH under Apache 2.0 license. The rights granted thereunder only apply to the weights and configuration files published in this repository. For the avoidance of doubt, any other artifacts not included in the repository are excluded from the license. The license especially does not extend to underlying code, model architecture, parameter settings or any training method." The repository ships the unmodified Apache License 2.0 text with no filled-in copyright line, and the card adds a General-Purpose AI Code of Practice point of contact for rightsholders. The card's Responsible Use section is guidance rather than a licence term: it opens by "Acknowledging the permissive nature of the license under which the weights of Kolibri are released" and asks users to refrain from unlawful use, so it adds no mandatory restriction to the artefacts the licence covers. The classification is of the published weights and configuration files, not of training code, data, or methods, which Aleph Alpha retains.

license_evidence.scope: The weights and configuration files published in the Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1 repository; the model card states the licence does not extend to code, model architecture, parameter settings, or training methods, which Aleph Alpha retains

access_boundary: This record represents the Kolibri 1 release of 3 October 2026, the version whose weights are published as Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1 and whose serving parsers are named kolibri1. It excludes Kolibri Origin, the earlier pipeline-validating iteration the developer states had "no public release"; the Pharia enterprise platform and any managed endpoint, since no first-party API is documented for this release; the aleph-alpha-inference serving package, which is a separate repository; and any downstream fine-tune, quantization, or re-upload of these weights.
strengths: Developer-published FP8 safetensors weights under Apache 2.0 with the licence scope stated in the model card itself, covering the repository's weights and configuration files and expressly excluding code, architecture, and training methods

A 189-page technical report and a model card that document the full pipeline, including 768 B200 GPUs over 21 days of pre-training, the bilingual data mix, more than 1.2M reinforcement-learning tasks, energy consumption, and per-checkpoint evaluation across safety, grounding, and abstention

A documented first-party serving path: an aleph-alpha-inference package with a ghcr.io container image, a vLLM serve command using the Kolibri reasoning and tool-call parsers, recommended sampling parameters, and an OpenAI-compatible local endpoint
tradeoffs: The full 78B model must be resident even though 3.46B parameters activate per token, so the documented minimum is 2x A100 80 GB, 2x H100 SXM5, or one H200, B200, or B300
The developer recommends contexts of at most 262,144 tokens for serving efficiency and complex tasks even though 1,048,576 tokens has been validated, and longer contexts need explicit vLLM overrides
No first-party managed API is documented for this release; access beyond the weights is enterprise deployment through sales contact, and no third-party hosting path is documented
Implicit knowledge stops at 18 June 2026 for both German and English, so deployments without tool access work from a dated world model

source_metadata.name: Kolibri 1
source_metadata.description: Kolibri is Aleph Alpha's mixture-of-experts (MoE) reasoning model, with a focus on German and English. The model supports an explicit reasoning mode and tool calling. It is optimized for long-context and inference efficiency.
